newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude prices edge up late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude prices edge up late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices edged up late, with future gains offset by bearish sentiment following reports the U.S. was close to accepting the Iraqi pricing formula under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
Forecasts of colder weather sent January crude prices 51 cents a barrel higher to $23.84.
Outright prices climbed at a slower pace for spot West Texas Intermediate crude (WTI).
WTI rose 15 cents and lifted the West Coast benchmark, Alaska North Slope (ANS), by the same amount.
West Coast traders said local spot markets remained thin, with ANS discounts flat at $2.20 under Dec WTI.
They cited weak margins and high crude prices for the meager buying interest.
Sellers of ANS kept offers at $1.90 under WTI and had no intention of selling at $2.20 discounts, they said.
Refinery buyers eyed Canadian crude altenatives to ANS, with two 450,000 barrel cargoes heard offered into the U.S. Northwest.
One cargo comprised Rainbow crude and the other, Koch Alberta. Both are slated for January delivery, but prospective buyers declined to specify prices.
Texaco Inc said Thursday its 20-inch California crude line remained under repair after a rupture Tueday.
Texaco said earlier a portion of the line, which links Bakersfield oil fields to refineries in San Francisco, shut automatically but would likely return Wednesday.
The line has a 340,000 barrel-per-day throughput.
Traders said rumors of no apportionment on Line 63 next month caused a flurry of offers for Line 63, a blended crude which can substitute for ANS.
Traders said a late Thursday coker fire at Mobil's Torrance refinery would add heavy crude supply to the market.
"If they shut down a coker, they're not going to run much crude," a trader said.

No new deals were reported for heavier grades. Kern River was at flat to 10 cents above posted prices, or around $17.00/10, while Line 63 was assessed 95 cents to $1.05 above postings or $3.20 to $3.00 under December WTI.
